module_title: Mechanics II - Rotational Motion & Gravitation (Basic / Foundational)
introduction: This level introduces the core principles of Rotational Motion and Gravitation. It covers how the laws of linear motion translate into rotational equivalents and explores how masses attract each other across the universe.

core_concepts.title: Center of Mass (COM)
core_concepts.description: The unique point where the entire mass of a system can be assumed to be concentrated. In the absence of external forces, the velocity of the center of mass remains constant.

core_concepts.title: Rotational Kinematics
core_concepts.description: The rotational equivalents of linear variables: Displacement ($\theta$), Velocity ($\omega$), and Acceleration ($\alpha$). For constant angular acceleration, equations mirror linear ones: $\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t$.

core_concepts.title: Newton's Law of Gravitation
core_concepts.description: The attractive force between any two bodies in the universe is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them: $F = G(m_1 m_2)/r^2$.

core_concepts.title: Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion
core_concepts.description: 1. Law of Orbits (Elliptical paths). 2. Law of Areas (Areal velocity is constant, proving conservation of angular momentum). 3. Law of Periods ($T^2 \propto r^3$).

important_entities.name: Universal Gravitational Constant ($G$)
important_entities.significance: It remains strictly constant throughout the universe and does not depend on the intervening medium between masses.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Gravitation is the universal force of attraction between ANY two bodies, whereas Gravity specifically refers to the attractive force exerted by a massive body (like Earth) on an object near its surface.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Square of Time is Cube of Radius ($T^2 \propto r^3$)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Most NEET questions comparing planetary distances and time periods can be solved instantly using the ratio: $(T_1/T_2)^2 = (r_1/r_2)^3$.

exam_strategy_tips: Gravitational force is ALWAYS attractive in nature; it never repels.
Only use the rotational kinematic equations if the angular acceleration ($\alpha$) is explicitly stated or derived to be constant.
